harvard-cs50-ai.about:
CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python (CS50 AI), taught by Brian Yu and David J. Malan at Harvard, explores the concepts and algorithms at the foundation of modern artificial intelligence: graph search, knowledge and logic, uncertainty and probability, optimisation, machine learning, neural networks and natural-language processing. Each of the seven weeks ends with a hands-on project, such as a game-playing AI, a Bayesian network or a neural-network image classifier.

The course is free via OpenCourseWare, with projects submitted online for feedback and a free CS50 certificate for completing all of them; a verified certificate is available through edX. Prerequisite: CS50x or at least a year of Python experience.

It is an excellent next step after CS50x or CS50P for students preparing for the International Olympiad in AI, AI research projects or university study in computer science.
highlights: Seven hands-on AI projects
Covers search, ML, neural networks and NLP
Free CS50 certificate
harvard-cs50-ai.eligibility: Anyone with CS50x completed or about one year of Python experience. Free edX and GitHub accounts needed. English.
how_to_apply: Check you meet the prerequisite (CS50x or Python experience).
Open cs50.harvard.edu/ai and set up your edX and GitHub accounts.
Watch each lecture and submit the week's project.
Complete all projects to receive the free CS50 certificate.
harvard-cs50-ai.costs: Free; optional paid edX verified certificate.

harvard-cs50-web.about:
CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript continues where CS50x leaves off, teaching the design and implementation of web apps. Topics include HTML and CSS, Git, Python, Django, SQL with models and migrations, JavaScript, user interfaces, testing and CI/CD, and scalability and security, across nine weeks of lectures and projects (for example a search engine front-end, a wiki, an e-commerce auction site and a social network).

It is free through OpenCourseWare; projects are submitted for feedback, and completing them all earns a free CS50 certificate (verified certificate optional via edX). Prerequisite: CS50x or prior experience in any programming language.

Students who complete it can build and deploy real websites, which is useful for school projects, startups and internships.
highlights: Django, SQL and JavaScript projects
Builds deployable web apps
Free CS50 certificate
harvard-cs50-web.eligibility: Anyone with CS50x or prior programming experience. Free edX and GitHub accounts needed. English.
how_to_apply: Open cs50.harvard.edu/web and read the project submission instructions.
Set up free edX and GitHub accounts.
Complete each week's project.
Submit the final project to qualify for the CS50 certificate.
harvard-cs50-web.costs: Free; optional paid edX verified certificate.

mit-opencourseware.about:
MIT OpenCourseWare (OCW) publishes the materials from more than 2,500 Massachusetts Institute of Technology courses for free: syllabi, lecture notes, full video lectures for many courses, problem sets with solutions and past exams. Subjects range across mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering, economics, biology, humanities and more. Popular starting points for school students include 18.01 Single Variable Calculus, 8.01 Classical Mechanics, 6.0001 Introduction to Computer Science and Programming in Python, and the 'OCW Highlights for High School' collection.

There is no registration, no enrolment and no certificate: you simply open a course and learn at your own pace, and materials are licensed under Creative Commons so teachers can reuse them. Students who want graded, certified versions of some MIT courses can look for MITx courses on edX.

OCW is an outstanding free resource for olympiad preparation, independent study projects and getting a feel for university-level work before applying.
highlights: 2,500+ MIT courses with notes, problem sets and exams
No sign-up needed; Creative Commons licensed
High-school highlights collection
mit-opencourseware.eligibility: Anyone. No registration. English (some translations exist).
how_to_apply: Go to ocw.mit.edu and search by subject or course number.
Start with an introductory course (e.g. 18.01, 8.01 or 6.0001) or the High School highlights.
Watch lectures and do the problem sets, checking against posted solutions.
For a certificate, look for the matching MITx course on edX.

khan-academy.about:
Khan Academy is a non-profit offering free, world-class education: thousands of videos and interactive exercises covering mathematics (from arithmetic to calculus, statistics and linear algebra), physics, chemistry, biology, computer programming, economics, history, grammar and test preparation. Courses are mapped to curricula including AP courses, and progress is tracked with mastery points so you can see exactly what to practise next.

Khan Academy also offers free SAT practice, which the College Board lists among its official practice resources ('How to Use Khan Academy'), alongside the full-length practice tests in the Bluebook app. Much content is available in several languages through Khan Academy's localised sites.

It is the single best free resource for filling gaps before olympiads, IB/A-level exams, the SAT or the first year of university maths and science.
highlights: Free practice and videos from primary school to early university
Mastery tracking and personalised practice
Available in many languages
khan-academy.eligibility: Anyone, any age. Free account recommended to save progress (under-13s sign up with a parent or teacher).
how_to_apply: Go to khanacademy.org and create a free learner account.
Choose your course (e.g. Algebra 2, AP Physics, Computer Programming) or take a course challenge to find your level.
Practise daily and use mastery goals to track progress.
Teachers can create free classes to assign work.

unicef-agora-courses.about:
Agora is UNICEF's global hub for learning. It is free and open to everyone who wants to make a positive difference in the lives of children: UNICEF staff, partners and the general public. The catalogue includes self-paced e-learning courses, learning journeys and resources on topics such as children's rights, child protection, education in emergencies, early childhood development, health and nutrition, gender, adolescent participation, data and innovation.

You register for free and can enrol at any time. Most public courses are short (from under an hour to a few hours), many are available in several languages (including Arabic), and many award a downloadable certificate of completion. These certificates are a meaningful addition to a CV for volunteering, youth-leadership, MUN or development-studies applications.

Agora is a good fit for students interested in international development, human rights, education or public health, and for youth volunteers who want recognised training.
highlights: Free courses from UNICEF, open to the public
Certificates of completion on many courses
Courses in Arabic, English, French and Spanish
unicef-agora-courses.eligibility: Anyone; free registration. Some courses are restricted to UNICEF staff or partners, but the public catalogue is open to all.
how_to_apply: Go to agora.unicef.org and click 'Register for free'.
Browse the catalogue and filter for courses open to the public in your language.
Enrol and complete the modules and any final quiz.
Download your certificate of completion from your profile.

un-cc-learn-climate-courses.about:
UN CC:Learn is a partnership of more than 30 UN agencies, with a secretariat at UNITAR in Geneva, that supports climate-change learning. Its e-learning platform offers self-paced and moderated courses on climate change basics, climate science, adaptation, climate finance, gender and climate, children and climate, sustainable diets, circular and green economy, and climate negotiations, many available in multiple languages including Arabic.

Courses are open to anyone with a free account. Learners who pass the final assessment can earn a UN certificate; the catalogue shows, for each course, whether a certificate is included and its cost (some certificates are now USD 30, while course content stays free).

These courses are ideal preparation for climate-themed MUN committees, environmental competitions (such as The Earth Prize) and youth climate projects, and the certificate signals genuine engagement to universities.
highlights: Content from 30+ UN agencies
Certificates for passing learners (some with a fee)
Many languages, including Arabic
un-cc-learn-climate-courses.eligibility: Anyone with a free account. Courses in several UN languages.
how_to_apply: Register for free at unccelearn.org.
Browse the course catalogue (start with 'Introduction to Climate Change').
Complete the modules and pass the final quiz.
Download the certificate (check the course page for any certificate fee).
un-cc-learn-climate-courses.costs: Courses free; some certificates cost USD 30 (shown per course).

sdg-academy-courses.about:
The SDG Academy is the education initiative of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN). It creates free, open educational resources on the Sustainable Development Goals with leading academics and practitioners, for example courses on the age of sustainable development (with economist Jeffrey Sachs), climate action, planetary health, food systems, human rights, early childhood development and sustainable cities.

Courses are free to take on the SDG Academy's own library and via partner platforms such as edX, where paid verified certificates are optional. The academy also links to master's programmes and professional certificates for those going further.

For secondary and university students, these courses are excellent background for development economics, MUN, essay competitions and social-impact projects.
highlights: Courses by leading SDG experts
Free; optional paid certificates on partner platforms
Covers all 17 SDGs
sdg-academy-courses.eligibility: Anyone; university-level content suitable for strong secondary students. English, with subtitles in some courses.
how_to_apply: Go to sdgacademy.org and browse the course library.
Choose a course and follow the link to enrol (free).
Complete the video lectures and readings at your own pace.
Optionally buy a verified certificate on the partner platform.
sdg-academy-courses.costs: Free; optional verified certificates on partner platforms cost extra.

openwho-courses.about:
OpenWHO is the World Health Organization's interactive, web-based knowledge-transfer platform. It offers free online courses on health emergencies and outbreaks, infectious diseases, vaccination, mental health, clinical management, and public-health skills, created by WHO experts. Courses are available in many languages, including Arabic and other UN languages, and many are designed for frontline responders as well as the general public.

Anyone can register free and enrol at any time. Courses are short and self-paced; learners who complete the assessments usually receive a free Record of Achievement or Confirmation of Participation.

For students interested in medicine, global health or WHO-themed MUN committees, OpenWHO provides authoritative, certified learning straight from the source.
highlights: Courses from WHO experts
Free certificates (Record of Achievement)
Dozens of languages
how_to_apply: Go to openwho.org and register for free.
Search the course catalogue by topic or language.
Enrol, complete the modules and pass the assessment.
Download your Record of Achievement.

world-bank-open-learning-campus.about:
The Open Learning Campus (OLC) is the World Bank Group's learning platform, offering e-learning courses, webinars and talks on development topics: poverty and inequality, public finance, education and health systems, climate change and disaster risk, energy, infrastructure, governance, gender, and data and evaluation. Many self-paced e-courses are free to the public and award a certificate on completion of the assessments.

You need to create a free account to enrol (the site opens with a sign-in page). Content is aimed at policymakers and development professionals, so it is best for university students or ambitious secondary students interested in economics, public policy or international relations.

OLC courses provide authoritative background for economics essays, MUN committees on development, and applications to economics or policy degrees.
highlights: Courses by World Bank experts
Free certificates on many self-paced courses
Development economics, climate and policy topics
world-bank-open-learning-campus.eligibility: Anyone with a free account; some content restricted to staff or partners. Mostly English, with some French, Spanish and Arabic.
how_to_apply: Go to olc.worldbank.org and create a free account.
Filter the catalogue for self-paced courses open to the public.
Enrol and complete the modules and final assessment.
Download your certificate.

elements-of-ai.about:
Elements of AI is a free online course created by the University of Helsinki and MinnaLearn to teach the basics of artificial intelligence to anyone. Its six chapters explain what AI is, problem solving with search, real-world AI and probability, machine learning, neural networks, and the implications of AI for society, using clear explanations and exercises rather than programming. A follow-up course, Building AI, introduces simple Python implementations.

The course is self-paced, available in many languages (with national versions across Europe and a global English version), and has been completed by more than 2 million people. Completing the exercises earns a free certificate from the University of Helsinki (and, for students at some institutions, ECTS credits).

It is an ideal first step for students curious about AI, and a credible certificate to show interest in AI ethics or technology on a university application.
highlights: Free certificate from the University of Helsinki
No maths or coding required
Many language versions
how_to_apply: Go to elementsofai.com and choose the Global (English) or your country's version.
Create a free account.
Complete the six chapters and their exercises.
Download your certificate; continue with Building AI if you want to code.

microsoft-learn-training.about:
Microsoft Learn is Microsoft's free learning platform. It offers thousands of short, interactive modules grouped into learning paths, covering AI fundamentals, Azure cloud, data analysis, Power BI, Python and C#, GitHub, cybersecurity and Microsoft 365 tools, often with free sandbox environments for practice. Learners earn badges and trophies on their Microsoft Learn profile.

Learning is free with a Microsoft account. Learning paths map to Microsoft role-based certifications (for example AI-900 Azure AI Fundamentals); exams are paid, but students sometimes access discounted vouchers through school or Microsoft programmes.

It is a practical way to build job-ready tech skills and a verifiable learning record.
highlights: Thousands of free interactive modules
Free practice sandboxes
Paths aligned to Microsoft certifications
microsoft-learn-training.eligibility: Anyone with a free Microsoft account.
how_to_apply: Go to learn.microsoft.com/training and sign in with a free Microsoft account.
Pick a learning path (e.g. AI or cloud fundamentals).
Complete the modules and knowledge checks to earn badges.
Optionally book a certification exam.
microsoft-learn-training.costs: Training free; certification exams are paid.

freecodecamp-certifications.about:
freeCodeCamp is a non-profit that has helped millions of people learn to code for free. Its interactive curriculum runs in the browser and leads to free certifications, including Responsive Web Design, JavaScript, Front End Libraries, Back End and APIs, Relational Databases, Python, Data Analysis with Python, Machine Learning with Python and more. Each certification requires completing required projects that you build yourself.

There are no fees and no deadlines; you sign in with a free account and progress is saved. freeCodeCamp also hosts thousands of free articles and full-length video courses (including CS50 courses on its YouTube channel).

Completed certifications are verifiable online and the projects form a portfolio, useful for internships and for showing initiative on university applications.
highlights: Free verifiable certifications
Project-based curriculum
No deadlines
how_to_apply: Go to freecodecamp.org/learn and create a free account.
Choose a certification path (start with Responsive Web Design or Python).
Complete the lessons and required projects.
Claim your certification from your profile.

yale-science-of-well-being-coursera.about:
The Science of Well-Being is Yale University's most popular online course, taught by psychology professor Laurie Santos. Over six modules it explains common misconceptions about happiness (money, grades, possessions), the biases that make our minds mislead us, and the research-based strategies that actually improve well-being, such as gratitude, social connection, exercise, sleep and savouring. Learners complete a 'rewirement' challenge, practising one habit for several weeks.

More than 5 million people have enrolled. The course takes about 10 hours, is self-paced, and has subtitles in 24 languages; Yale also offers a teen version for younger students.

It is a great choice for students handling exam stress or university applications, and an easy, respected certificate for any CV.
highlights: Yale's most popular course; 5M+ learners
Evidence-based habits for happiness and stress
Subtitles in 24 languages; teen version available
yale-science-of-well-being-coursera.eligibility: Anyone; no prerequisites. Free Coursera account required.
how_to_apply: Open the course page on coursera.org and click 'Enroll'.
Choose the free option (or apply for financial aid if you want the certificate).
Complete the six modules and the habit-building 'rewirement' exercise.
If enrolled for a certificate, finish the graded assignments to receive it.
yale-science-of-well-being-coursera.costs: Free to enrol and study the course materials (Coursera audit/preview options vary by course). A shareable certificate requires payment or Coursera Plus; Coursera offers financial aid on eligible courses through an application on the course page.

learning-how-to-learn-coursera.about:
Learning How to Learn: Powerful mental tools to help you master tough subjects gives practical, neuroscience-based techniques used by experts in art, music, literature, maths, science and sport. It covers focused and diffuse modes of thinking, chunking, spaced repetition, the Pomodoro technique for procrastination, memory techniques, and how to prepare for tests. The instructors are Dr Barbara Oakley and Professor Terrence Sejnowski (Salk Institute / UC San Diego).

More than 4 million learners have enrolled; the course is beginner level, self-paced, and available with subtitles in 25 languages, with fully translated Portuguese and Spanish versions.

It is one of the best investments a student can make before exams, olympiad training or a demanding university course.
highlights: 4M+ learners; beginner level
Techniques for focus, memory and procrastination
Subtitles in 25 languages
learning-how-to-learn-coursera.eligibility: Anyone; no prerequisites. Free Coursera account required.
how_to_apply: Open the course on coursera.org and click 'Enroll'.
Choose the free option or apply for financial aid for a certificate.
Work through the four modules and quizzes.
Apply the techniques to your current studies.
learning-how-to-learn-coursera.costs: Free to enrol and study the course materials (Coursera audit/preview options vary by course). A shareable certificate requires payment or Coursera Plus; Coursera offers financial aid on eligible courses through an application on the course page.

stanford-deeplearningai-machine-learning.about:
The Machine Learning Specialization, created by Stanford Online and DeepLearning.AI and taught by AI pioneer Andrew Ng, is the updated version of his famous Stanford machine-learning course. Its three courses cover supervised learning (linear and logistic regression), advanced learning algorithms (neural networks with TensorFlow, decision trees, practical advice for building ML systems) and unsupervised learning, recommender systems and reinforcement learning. Each week includes optional and graded Jupyter notebook labs in Python.

The programme is beginner-friendly (high-school algebra and basic Python suffice), takes about two months at 10 hours a week, and has subtitles in 30 languages; more than 850,000 learners have enrolled.

It is a recognised first credential in machine learning and excellent preparation for the International Olympiad in AI or AI research projects.
highlights: Taught by Andrew Ng
Hands-on Python and TensorFlow labs
Shareable certificate from Stanford Online & DeepLearning.AI
stanford-deeplearningai-machine-learning.eligibility: Anyone with basic Python and high-school maths. Free Coursera account.
how_to_apply: Open the specialization on coursera.org and click 'Enroll for free'.
Start with Course 1 (Supervised Machine Learning) and follow the weekly schedule.
Apply for financial aid on each course if you need the certificate but cannot pay.
Complete all graded labs to earn the specialization certificate.
stanford-deeplearningai-machine-learning.costs: Free to enrol and study the course materials (Coursera audit/preview options vary by course). A shareable certificate requires payment or Coursera Plus; Coursera offers financial aid on eligible courses through an application on the course page.

umich-python-for-everybody.about:
Python for Everybody is a five-course specialization from the University of Michigan taught by Professor Charles 'Dr Chuck' Severance. It starts with the basics of programming (variables, loops, functions), then moves to Python data structures, accessing web data (HTML, XML, JSON, APIs), using databases with SQL, and a capstone project retrieving, processing and visualising data.

It assumes no prior programming experience, takes about two months at 10 hours a week, and has subtitles in 27 languages. More than 2 million learners have enrolled.

It is one of the most beginner-friendly routes into programming and data analysis, and suits students who want practical skills for science projects, economics or computing.
highlights: 2M+ learners; no experience needed
Covers web data, SQL databases and visualisation
Shareable University of Michigan certificate
how_to_apply: Open the specialization on coursera.org and click 'Enroll for free'.
Begin with 'Programming for Everybody (Getting Started with Python)'.
Apply for financial aid if you want certificates without paying.
Complete the five courses and the capstone.
umich-python-for-everybody.costs: Free to enrol and study the course materials (Coursera audit/preview options vary by course). A shareable certificate requires payment or Coursera Plus; Coursera offers financial aid on eligible courses through an application on the course page.

yale-financial-markets-coursera.about:
Financial Markets, taught by Yale professor and Nobel laureate Robert Shiller, gives an overview of the ideas, methods and institutions that let society manage risk and foster enterprise. Topics include risk management and insurance, the Capital Asset Pricing Model, efficient markets and behavioural finance, stocks, bonds and real estate, central banks and monetary policy, investment banking, and the ethics of finance.

The course is beginner level, self-paced, and has more than 2.4 million learners with subtitles in 22 languages.

It is excellent preparation for economics or finance degrees, essay competitions in economics, and investment challenges.
highlights: Taught by Nobel laureate Robert Shiller
Beginner level; 2.4M+ learners
Covers insurance, banking, behavioural finance
how_to_apply: Open the course on coursera.org and click 'Enroll'.
Choose the free option or apply for financial aid for the certificate.
Complete the seven modules and quizzes.
yale-financial-markets-coursera.costs: Free to enrol and study the course materials (Coursera audit/preview options vary by course). A shareable certificate requires payment or Coursera Plus; Coursera offers financial aid on eligible courses through an application on the course page.

deeplearningai-ai-for-everyone.about:
AI For Everyone, created by DeepLearning.AI and taught by Andrew Ng, explains artificial intelligence for non-engineers: common AI terminology (machine learning, deep learning, data science), what AI can realistically do, how to choose and run AI projects, how AI fits into companies, and the ethical and societal questions it raises.

The course takes about 7 hours over four modules, is beginner level and has subtitles in 27 languages; more than 2.6 million learners have enrolled.

It gives students the vocabulary to discuss AI in essays, debates and MUN committees and is a gentle introduction before technical courses like CS50 AI or the Machine Learning Specialization.
highlights: Non-technical; about 7 hours
2.6M+ learners
Covers AI strategy and ethics
how_to_apply: Open the course on coursera.org and click 'Enroll'.
Choose the free option or apply for financial aid.
Complete the four modules.
deeplearningai-ai-for-everyone.costs: Free to enrol and study the course materials (Coursera audit/preview options vary by course). A shareable certificate requires payment or Coursera Plus; Coursera offers financial aid on eligible courses through an application on the course page.

fastai-practical-deep-learning.about:
Practical Deep Learning for Coders, by Jeremy Howard and fast.ai, teaches deep learning 'top-down': you build and deploy working models first and learn the theory as you go. Its nine lessons (about 90 minutes each) cover computer vision, natural-language processing, tabular data, collaborative filtering, and the foundations of neural networks, using PyTorch, fastai and Hugging Face libraries. A second part (30+ hours) goes deeper into the foundations of Stable Diffusion-style models.

It is free, needs no special hardware (it shows how to use free cloud notebooks), and does not require university maths, only some coding experience (ideally Python). It is based on the free online book 'Deep Learning for Coders with fastai and PyTorch'.

Many AI practitioners started here; it is ideal for students preparing AI projects, Kaggle competitions or the IOAI.
highlights: Free; no special hardware needed
Build and deploy models from lesson one
Uses PyTorch, fastai and Hugging Face
fastai-practical-deep-learning.eligibility: Anyone with about a year of coding experience (Python preferred).
how_to_apply: Go to course.fast.ai and read 'How do I get started?'.
Set up a free cloud notebook (e.g. Kaggle or Colab) as shown.
Watch each lesson and run the notebooks.
Join the fast.ai forums for help.

hugging-face-learn-courses.about:
Hugging Face, the open-source AI platform, publishes a set of free courses on its Learn hub: the LLM Course (transformers, fine-tuning and using language models with the Hugging Face ecosystem), the Agents Course (building and deploying AI agents), the Deep Reinforcement Learning Course, the Community Computer Vision Course, the Audio Course, a Robotics Course built on LeRobot, and short courses on post-training models.

Courses are self-paced, use Python and free notebooks, and several (such as the Agents and Deep RL courses) award free certificates for completing assignments.

They are ideal for students who already code in Python and want to build real projects with modern open-source AI models.
highlights: Courses on LLMs, agents, RL, vision, audio and robotics
Free; some award certificates
Hands-on with open-source models
hugging-face-learn-courses.eligibility: Anyone with Python experience; free Hugging Face account for certificates.
how_to_apply: Go to huggingface.co/learn and pick a course.
Create a free Hugging Face account.
Follow the units and run the notebooks.
Complete the assignments to receive a certificate where offered.

un-women-training-centre-elearning.about:
The UN Women Training Centre eLearning Campus is a global online platform for training on gender equality and women's empowerment, open to everybody interested in using training as a means of transformation. Courses range from the self-paced introductory series 'I Know Gender' (gender concepts, international frameworks, and gender in areas such as work, health, education and peace) to moderated, specialised courses for professionals.

The campus is available in English, Spanish, French and Arabic. You register for a free account; many self-paced courses are free and issue a certificate on completion, while some moderated courses have fees or are for UN staff.

These courses help students working on human-rights projects, MUN committees (UN Women, CSW, UNHRC) and youth leadership programmes.
highlights: Free 'I Know Gender' course with certificate
Available in Arabic, English, French and Spanish
Run by UN Women
un-women-training-centre-elearning.eligibility: Anyone; free registration. Some moderated courses are fee-based or restricted.
how_to_apply: Go to trainingcentre.unwomen.org and click 'Register'.
Search the course catalogue for self-paced free courses (start with I Know Gender).
Complete the modules and assessment.
Download your certificate.
un-women-training-centre-elearning.costs: Many self-paced courses free; some moderated courses charge fees.

saylor-academy-free-courses.about:
Saylor Academy is a non-profit that has offered free, self-paced online courses since 2008, with more than 3 million students enrolled. Its catalogue of 160+ courses covers business administration, computer science, mathematics (from pre-calculus to calculus and statistics), science, social sciences, arts and humanities, and English as a second language, plus specialization programmes. Courses use open educational resources and end with a final exam; passing earns a free certificate.

Some Saylor courses are recommended for college credit by external evaluators, and Saylor offers degree programmes for those who want to go further.

For students, it is a structured, free way to study a subject in depth (for example to prepare for AP, A-level or first-year university courses) with proof of completion.
highlights: 160+ free courses; 3M+ students
Free certificates after a final exam
Enrol anytime
how_to_apply: Go to learn.saylor.org and sign up.
Browse by subject and enrol in a course.
Work through the units at your own pace.
Pass the final exam to receive a free certificate.

google-machine-learning-crash-course.about:
Machine Learning Crash Course (MLCC) is Google's free introduction to machine learning, relied on by millions of people since 2018 and refreshed with a stronger focus on interactive learning. Self-contained modules cover ML models (linear and logistic regression, classification), working with data (numerical and categorical data, datasets, generalisation and overfitting), advanced models (neural networks, embeddings, large language models) and real-world ML (production systems, AutoML, fairness).

Each module combines short videos, interactive visualisations and programming exercises in Colab notebooks. It is free and needs only a Google account for the exercises; there is no formal certificate.

It is a fast, credible way to understand how ML works before IOAI preparation, a research project or the Stanford/DeepLearning.AI specialization.
highlights: Free; interactive visualisations and Colab exercises
Covers neural networks, embeddings and LLMs
Responsible-AI module
google-machine-learning-crash-course.eligibility: Anyone with high-school algebra and basic Python.
how_to_apply: Open developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course.
Check the prerequisites page and start with the ML Models modules.
Do the interactive exercises and Colab notebooks.

cisco-netacad-python-essentials.about:
Cisco Networking Academy (NetAcad) is one of the world's largest IT-skills programmes, offering online courses through its own platform and partner schools. Its free self-paced catalogue includes Python Essentials 1 (no prior experience necessary), Introduction to Cybersecurity, Networking Basics, Introduction to IoT, Introduction to Data Science and more.

Python Essentials 1, developed with the OpenEDG Python Institute, teaches programming fundamentals and prepares learners for the entry-level PCEP certification exam (exam is separate and paid). Completers of NetAcad courses earn shareable Cisco digital badges.

NetAcad is a practical path to job-ready IT and cybersecurity skills, and many secondary schools and universities worldwide teach its courses in class.
highlights: Free Python, cybersecurity and networking courses
Cisco digital badges on completion
Prepares for certifications such as PCEP
cisco-netacad-python-essentials.eligibility: Anyone; free account. No prerequisites for introductory courses.
how_to_apply: Go to netacad.com and create a free account.
Enrol in Python Essentials 1 (or another free self-paced course).
Complete the modules, labs and final test.
Claim your digital badge; optionally book a certification exam.
cisco-netacad-python-essentials.costs: Free courses; certification exams cost extra.

maharat-min-google.about:
Maharat min Google (Skills from Google) is Google's free digital-skills programme for the Middle East and North Africa, run under Grow with Google. It offers Arabic-language courses for individuals and business owners: job preparation, communication and productivity, digital marketing, programming and development, AI basics, cloud computing basics, online safety, design and sustainability. Introductory courses are hosted on Google's Skillshop catalogue, with more advanced cloud learning on Google Skills.

The site also links to Google Career Certificates (IT support, data analytics, UX design and more), which are professional programmes delivered through Coursera; these are paid but often available through scholarships and financial aid.

For Arabic-speaking students, it is one of the easiest ways to learn practical digital and AI skills in their own language.
highlights: Free courses in Arabic
Digital marketing, coding, AI and cloud basics
Links to Google Career Certificates
maharat-min-google.eligibility: Anyone; free Google account. Content focused on Arabic speakers.
how_to_apply: Go to grow.google (Arabic MENA site) and open the course catalogue.
Pick a free course (e.g. AI basics or digital marketing) and sign in with a Google account.
Complete the lessons and quizzes.
For a Google Career Certificate, follow the link to the certificate page and apply for financial aid if needed.
maharat-min-google.costs: Introductory courses free; Google Career Certificates are paid (financial aid available via Coursera).

aws-educate.about:
AWS Educate is Amazon Web Services' free programme for learning cloud computing. It is open to anyone, regardless of education level or experience: learners aged 13 and up can register with only an email address (the job board is for 18+). It offers a self-paced library of beginner videos and hands-on labs where you practise real cloud skills, covering storage (Amazon S3), compute (Amazon EC2), networking (Amazon VPC), databases (Amazon RDS) and cloud operations, as well as AI and machine-learning topics.

Completing learning content earns shareable digital badges. No credit card is required.

Cloud skills are increasingly expected in computer-science and data careers; AWS Educate is a safe, free sandbox to start.

Hands-on labs without a credit card
Shareable digital badges
aws-educate.eligibility: Anyone aged 13+ with an email address.

Choose a learning path and complete the labs.
Collect your digital badges.

mit-open-learning-library.about:
MIT Open Learning Library hosts selected MIT course materials in an interactive format: unlike OpenCourseWare's static files, its courses include auto-graded problems, so learners get immediate feedback. Courses come from departments including physics, mathematics, electrical engineering and computer science, materials science, management, urban studies and writing, many of them archived versions of MITx courses.

All resources are free to use and available to learners worldwide without registration; the library does not offer certificates.

It is ideal for self-motivated students who want MIT-level practice with feedback, for example in calculus, mechanics or introductory programming.

Free, no registration
Physics, maths, CS, engineering
mit-open-learning-library.eligibility: Anyone. No registration (optional account to save progress).
how_to_apply: Go to openlearninglibrary.mit.edu.
Search or filter by department.
Open a course and work through the exercises at your own pace.

harvard-free-online-courses.about:
Harvard University maintains an official online learning catalogue that lets you filter for free courses. It includes HarvardX courses (many free to audit on edX), CS50 courses, and offerings from Harvard schools such as Arts & Sciences, Public Health, Medicine, Education and the Divinity School. Subjects range from computer science and data science to humanities, health and medicine, social sciences, mathematics, education and business.

Each listing states the format, length and start date (many are self-paced and 'available anytime') and links to the enrolment page. Free courses typically let you learn all content at no cost, with an optional paid verified certificate on the hosting platform.

It is the most reliable place to find genuine Harvard courses for free, useful for exploring a subject before choosing a university major.

Courses from many Harvard schools
Most self-paced; optional paid certificates
harvard-free-online-courses.eligibility: Anyone; enrolment rules vary by hosting platform (usually a free edX account).

uwc-spain-action-for-peace-toledo-2026.about:
ActionxPeace is UWC Spain's experiential peace-education programme. Sixty teenagers from different countries and backgrounds live together for five days and work on identity, empathy, coexistence, conflict transformation and peacebuilding through workshops, dialogue, outdoor activities and community life. Participants leave with practical conflict-transformation tools and a sense of their own role as changemakers.

It is one of the few international residential programmes aimed at secondary-school students rather than adults, and a good taste of the United World Colleges approach to education for peace.

The seminar is organised by UWC Spain and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Nambroca (Toledo), Spain on 4 December 2026 – 8 December 2026. It is for 60 participants. Who it is for: young people born between 2009 and 2011 (aged about 15–17) from diverse backgrounds, plus youth leaders. Participants must be residents of: all countries: Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries neighbouring the EU and other countries in the world. Working language: English and Spanish (bilingual programme).

Costs: Course fee €470, covering full-board shared accommodation at El Casar de la Inesa (Nambroca, Toledo), meals, materials and all activities. Ten need-based scholarships are available for Spanish and international participants. Travel is not reimbursed. Applications close on 31 October 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 23 November 2026.

salto-resilient-roots-facilitation-glari.about:
Resilient Roots trains youth workers to facilitate inclusive, trauma-informed group processes through embodiment, dialogue, nature connection and practical facilitation tools. Module I (8–15 November 2026, Facilitating Climate Dialogue Foundations) is listed here; Module II (Hosting Emergence, 13–20 December 2026) can be booked separately and requires Module I or a previous Pathways course.

The organiser asks applicants to write in their own words: applications written with AI are not considered.

It runs in Steckborn (Schloss Glarisegg), Switzerland on 8 November 2026 – 15 November 2026 (Module II on 13–20 December 2026 is optional). It is for 25–30 participants. Who it is for: youth workers, educators, activists and facilitators working with climate anxiety, uncertainty and group processes. Participants must be residents of: Romania, France, Italy, Denmark and Switzerland (the organiser accepts only these countries). Working language: English.

Costs: Sliding-scale participation contribution. Limited places funded by Movetia (the Swiss national agency) are available for eligible youth workers; self-funded participation is also possible. Accommodation, food and travel details are on the organiser's website (pathways-courses.org/resilient-roots). Sessions cover audience engagement, photography, visual storytelling, graphic content and social-media strategy, with the city of Cairo as the creative backdrop. salto-limitless-ngo-leadership-stara-zag.about:
LIMITLESS is built for people who wear too many hats: project coordinators, grant writers and founders stuck in reactive mode as funding and rules change. Over seven days, Synergy Bulgaria uses its coaching-based Synergy Method to help participants step out of firefighting, prevent burnout and redefine how they lead and create impact.

Synergy has run non-formal education and ESC volunteering programmes since 2013, and the course is aimed at people bringing real challenges from their organisations rather than general curiosity.

The training course is organised by Synergy Bulgaria and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Stara Zagora, Bulgaria on 11 November 2026 – 17 November 2026. It is for 24 participants. Who it is for: people aged 18+ who run or are in the core team of an NGO, or social entrepreneurs working on impact-driven projects; comfortable in English and able to attend all seven days. Participants must be residents of: Erasmus+ Programme countries. Working language: English.

Travel is reimbursed up to the Erasmus+ distance-band limit. Applications close on 8 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 9 November 2026.

enrmsc-equal-ground-q1-online-2026.about:
Equal Ground is ENRMSC's quarterly dialogue series. The first session asks what meaningful participation looks like when communities are not just invited to the table but can shape decisions, policies and action. Through contributions from people with lived experience and participatory exchange, participants look at barriers to participation, the role of youth workers and how organisations can turn community perspectives into action.

It is a short, practical entry point for anyone working on inclusion, migration or youth participation, and a way to meet the network behind the larger ENRMSC Forum in Warsaw in April 2027.

The online forum is organised by European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC) and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs online on 10 November 2026. It is for 50 participants. Who it is for: youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, community practitioners and people with lived experience of migration or statelessness. Participants must be residents of: all countries: Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries neighbouring the EU and other countries in the world. Working language: English.

Costs: Free of charge. Online, so no accommodation or travel is involved. Applications close on 9 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 10 November 2026.

It shows how arts and creativity can help communication and engagement, especially with young people who take part in different ways, and gives practical ideas for adapting activities and methods.

Participants also visit local organisations working on inclusion and diversity in Gdańsk. The aim is to give educators concrete arts-based methods to overcome communication barriers, encourage self-expression and adapt activities to people with different abilities, backgrounds and needs.

When Stories Collide asks how youth workers can handle difficult, polarising topics — including antisemitism and anti-Muslim hostility around the Israeli–Palestinian conflict — in schools, youth centres and camps. Over five working days participants reflect on their own positions and biases, try methods for dialogue that leave room for ambiguity (including a full-day Brave Space workshop), and analyse how social media and narratives shape young people's views.

The seminar is organised by BDKJ Mainz and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Wiesbaden, Germany on 10 December 2026 – 16 December 2026. It is for 10 participants. Who it is for: youth workers, youth leaders, project managers, coaches and teachers. Participants must be residents of: Germany and Israel only. Working language: English.

Costs: Participation fee €100 (€50 for students). Accommodation and food are included at no extra cost. No travel reimbursement. Applications close on 10 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 11 November 2026.

Off Script focuses on the step from being a participant in youth activities to being responsible for a group. Through experiential learning, observation and reflection, participants explore group dynamics, pedagogy, diversity and inclusion, conflict management, safeguarding and communication, and adapt methods through IYNF's green (environment), red (democracy) and blue (youth work) themes. They also learn to cater for a large group as part of a self-catering programme.

The training course is organised by International Young Naturefriends (IYNF) and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Bergen aan Zee (Het Zeehuis), Netherlands on 31 January 2027 – 5 February 2027. It is for 25 participants. Who it is for: young people who have taken part in non-formal education as participants and are ready to take their first steps as group leaders, facilitators or trainers. Participants must be residents of: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Netherlands, Portugal, Romania and Spain. Working language: English.

Costs: Participation fee €50 for Naturefriends members, €75 for non-members. Accommodation and plant-based (vegan) food provided; the course is self-catering, so participants cook together. Travel reimbursed under the IYNF travel policy. Youthpass certificate. Applications close on 13 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 16 November 2026.

melton-global-solvers-accelerator-2027.about:
The Global Solvers Accelerator is the Melton Foundation's programme for grassroots activists, social entrepreneurs, SDG practitioners, action researchers and community organisers. From 1 April to 30 November 2027 participants work online in peer groups on the real tensions in their projects, then meet for an in-person Co-Lab in Germany on 3–10 July 2027. The focus is less on showcasing a project and more on letting the process challenge and develop both the work and the person.

The accelerator programme is organised by Melton Foundation and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Online + Co-Lab in Germany, Germany on 1 April 2027 – 30 November 2027 (online April–November 2027; in-person Co-Lab in Germany, 3–10 July 2027). It is for a cohort of participants. Who it is for: changemakers aged 20–35 already running or co-leading a project, enterprise, research effort or community initiative tied to the SDGs, with a track record of social impact. Participants must be residents of: all countries: Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries neighbouring the EU and other countries in the world. Working language: English.

Costs: Programme fee USD 900, payable only if selected; it also feeds a fund that supports participants' projects afterwards. Need-based scholarships cover 20%, 50% or 80% of the fee (request it in the application). Travel, accommodation and meals for the in-person Co-Lab in Germany are fully covered. Applications close on 15 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 16 December 2026.

octopus-project-neurodiversity-online-20.about:
The Octopus Project supports more inclusive educational and pedagogical practice in youth work for neurodiverse people. In this two-hour online event the partners present their results, with a special focus on an educational board game, clarify key concepts, answer questions and explore future collaboration with participants.

esc-maximize-arts-creativity-thessalonik.about:
Arts and culture inspire, transform, and unite. At EERco, through the European Solidarity Corps, we harness this power to build a greener, more inclusive future. We open doors for young people with fewer opportunities to launch projects with strong social impact. In parks and public spaces, we merge creativity with sustainability—using recycled and reclaimed materials to upgrade outdoor areas and honor their history. Digital tools amplify our mission, tracking energy use, cutting waste, and sharing eco-friendly practices across communities. We nurture talented young artists who may lack resources and host lively events that spark dialogue on green living and social solidarity. Our actions uplift local neighborhoods, turning shared spaces into vibrant hubs of creativity and care.
